C: › [ C ] usually disapproving a large, angry crowd, especially one that could easily become violent
› [ C ] informal a group of people who are friends or who are similar in some way
S: › [ S ] informal an organization of criminals

T usually passive: › [ T usually passive ] to come together around someone in a crowd to express admiration, interest, or anger

I or T: › [ I or T ] When birds or small animals mob a bigger or more frightening bird or animal that is hunting them, they attack it together and force it to go away.
（鳥群或一群小動物）成群襲擊，圍攻（猛禽或猛獸）

example: The angry mob outside the jail was/were ready to riot.
監獄外憤怒的暴民準備鬧事。
a lynch mob
行私刑的暴民
50 people were killed in three days of mob violence.
三天的暴亂中有50人喪生。
The usual mob was/were hanging out at the bar.
酒吧裡閒混的還是往常那夥人。
a New York mob leader
紐約犯罪集團的頭目
See also
mobster
They were mobbed by fans when they arrived at the theatre.
他們到達劇院時，被影迷團團圍住。
Let's not go to that bar tonight - it's always mobbed (= there are always a lot of people there) on Fridays.
我們今晚不要去那個酒吧了——那裡星期五總是有許多人。

not usually before noun: › [ not usually before noun ] moving or walking around freely
› able to be moved from one place to another

NONE: › used to describe a service available on a mobile phone, small computer, etc.
（服務）可以在行動電話（或小型電腦）上提供的

C: A1 mainly UK US usually cell phone a
› a decoration or work of art that has many parts that move freely in the air, for example hanging from threads
風鈴；（可隨風擺動的）懸掛飾物

example: You've broken your ankle but you'll be fully mobile within a couple of months.
你摔斷了腳踝，但用不了幾個月你就可以行動自如了。
It's important to keep the joint mobile while it heals.
在關節痊癒時，保持關節活動是很重要的。
He uses a mobile laboratory.
他使用一個可移動的實驗室
a mobile medical unit
流動醫療單位
行動電話號碼（同 mobile number）
My mobile's 07796 10253.

NONE: › any piece of electronic equipment such as a mobile phone or small computer that you can use in different places
› a type of building that people live in, usually staying in one place, but able to be moved using a vehicle or sometimes its own engine
› a large road vehicle that travels around, especially in the countryside, carrying books for people to borrow
（尤指鄉村地區的）流動圖書館，行動圖書館車
› the number for your mobile phone
A1 a phone that is connected to the phone system by radio instead of by a wire, and can be used anywhere its signals can be received
行動電話，手機，手提電話

U: › the ability to move freely or be easily moved
› the ability to have particular services available on a mobile phone, small computer, etc.
可在移動設備上提供服務的能力

example: Some neck injuries cause total loss of mobility below the point of injury.
某些頸部損傷會導致受傷部位以下肢體完全喪失活動能力。
I prefer the mobility of a hand-held camera.
我更喜歡手提攝像機的靈活性。
See also
upward mobility (upwardly mobile)
Consumers are demanding mobility, so that they can have access to information wherever they go.
消費者要求移享有動設備上的服務，好讓他們隨處接觸資訊。

NONE: › a small vehicle like a motorcycle with three or four wheels and an electric engine, designed for people who cannot walk well

example: She is disabled, but can take her daughter to school using her mobility scooter.
她身有殘障，但是可以用她的電動代步車送女兒上學。

T: › [ T ] to organize or prepare something, such as a group of people, for a purpose
I or T: › [ I or T ] to prepare to fight, especially in a war

example: Representatives for all the main candidates are trying to mobilize voter support.
所有主要候選人的代表正在努力鼓動選民給予支持。
The government has mobilized several of the army's top combat units.
政府已調動了若干陸軍精銳作戰部隊。
Troops have been mobilizing for the past three weeks.
過去三個星期裡，部隊一直在備戰。

NONE: › an object with only one surface that is made by twisting a long strip of material once and then joining its two ends
梅比斯環（只有一個平面的物體，透過將長帶狀的物料扭轉一次，然後黏合兩端形成）
